original_question: Among all planar graphs on n >= 9 vertices, is the graph K_2 joined with the path P_{n-2} always the one with maximum spectral radius?
target_in_paper: Section 3, Conjecture 5: the Boots–Royle / Cao–Vince conjecture on the maximum adjacency spectral radius of an n-vertex planar graph, with extremal candidate K_2 ∨ P_{n-2}.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the right topic, ambient graph class, order parameter n, extremal object K_2 ∨ P_{n-2}, and the optimization target of maximum spectral radius. It is also aligned with the historical n ≥ 9 threshold usually attached to this conjecture.
missing_details: Clarify that 'spectral radius' means the largest eigenvalue ρ(G) of the adjacency matrix A(G), since the paper works with adjacency spectra unless otherwise specified.
State the paper-wide graph conventions: graphs are simple, undirected, and unweighted.
Make the quantifier fully explicit: for every integer n ≥ 9 and every planar graph G with |V(G)| = n.
State uniqueness explicitly, not only maximality: the intended question is whether K_2 ∨ P_{n-2} is the unique extremal graph.
Define K_2 ∨ P_{n-2} precisely as the join of K_2 and P_{n-2}, i.e. the graph obtained from K_2 ∪ P_{n-2} by adding all possible edges between the two parts.
Spell out that P_{n-2} is the path on n - 2 vertices.
No ambient field/ring, homogeneity, degree restriction, or nilpotency condition is relevant here; the omitted structure is graph-theoretic rather than algebraic.
refined_question: For every integer n ≥ 9, among all simple planar graphs G with |V(G)| = n, is the join K_2 ∨ P_{n-2}—obtained from K_2 ∪ P_{n-2} by adding all possible edges between the K_2-part and the path P_{n-2}—the unique graph with maximum adjacency spectral radius ρ(G), where ρ(G) denotes the largest eigenvalue of the adjacency matrix A(G)?
justification: The draft clearly targets the planar-graph extremal-spectral topic in Section 3 rather than the earlier conjectures on inequalities. The nearest official formulation in the paper is therefore Conjecture 5. The surrounding paragraph in Section 3 sets the exact problem as the maximum spectral radius problem for planar graphs and records the known partial progress for sufficiently large n, while the global preliminaries before Section 1 define the needed notation and conventions: graphs are simple, undirected, and unweighted; eigenvalues and spectral radius are those of the adjacency matrix; and the join notation and path notation are fixed there. So the paper-faithful sharpening is to make the adjacency operator, the join construction, the order condition, and uniqueness explicit, without broadening to hypergraphs or to more general F-free planar extremal problems.
